quizzes.title: Fuel Norms, Reports and Defence Tests
quizzes.passage:
Corporate Average Fuel Efficiency, or CAFE, norms are rules that set fuel efficiency standards for vehicles in India. The norms are designed to reduce fuel consumption, lower carbon dioxide emissions and curb air pollution. They apply to petrol, diesel, LPG, CNG, hybrid and electric passenger vehicles, and they are implemented in phases. Automobile manufacturers have pushed for relaxed emission standards compared with the CAFE-III norms.

Separately, the United Nations has released the seventh edition of its Global Environment Outlook, titled 'A Future We Choose'. The report states that the world is far off track from Paris Agreement targets. It also warns that pollution remains one of the largest environmental health risks, and that rapid land degradation threatens food security and biodiversity. The Outlook is described as a leading voice for planetary protection, and it defines the international environmental agenda.

In defence news, DRDO successfully tested the K-4 submarine-launched ballistic missile from INS Arighat. It also completed trials of the Akash-NG surface-to-air missile, which was produced in collaboration with Bharat Electronics Limited.

India also marks Antarctica Day on December 1, which commemorates the 1959 Antarctic Treaty. The treaty bans nuclear activities south of 60 degrees south latitude and preserves 10 per cent of Earth for peace and science.

questions.q: Under which Act are the CAFE norms notified?
options: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the CAFE norms are notified under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001.

questions.q: Which Ahom ruler established the Charaichung Royal Bird Sanctuary in 1633?
questions.explanation: The booklet credits Ahom ruler Pratap Singha with establishing the Charaichung Royal Bird Sanctuary in 1633.

questions.q: The Global Environment Outlook (GEO-7) is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the headquarters of GEO-7 as Nairobi, Kenya.

questions.q:
Read the two statements.
Assertion (A): Phase I of the CAFE norms, in 2017-18, set baseline efficiency targets for passenger vehicles.
Reason (R): Phase II of the CAFE norms, in 2022-23, introduced stricter fuel efficiency targets.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements match the booklet's phase descriptions, but the Phase II change does not explain the Phase I targets.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Siliserh Lake
II. Kopra Reservoir
III. Samudra Pratap
IV. BlueBird Block-2
A. Rajasthan
B. Chhattisgarh
C. Indian Coast Guard
D. AST SpaceMobile (USA)
questions.explanation: Siliserh Lake is in Rajasthan, Kopra Reservoir in Chhattisgarh, Samudra Pratap was inducted by the Indian Coast Guard, and BlueBird Block-2 was built for AST SpaceMobile.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Majuli is recognised as the world's largest river island.
II. Phase III of the CAFE norms covers the years 2027-32.
III. Phase I of the CAFE norms was implemented in 2022-23.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while Phase I was in 2017-18, not 2022-23.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Pollution is linked to 9 million deaths every year.
II. BlueBird Block-2 was placed into Low Earth Orbit by the LVM3-M6 launch.
III. Samudra Pratap is India's first hydrogen fuel-cell passenger vessel.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are in the booklet, while Samudra Pratap is a pollution control vessel, not the hydrogen fuel-cell passenger vessel.

quizzes.title: Wetlands, Satellites and Heritage Facts
quizzes.passage:
India has added two wetlands, Siliserh Lake and Kopra Reservoir, to the Ramsar List of wetlands of international importance. Siliserh Lake is located in Alwar, Rajasthan, while Kopra Reservoir is in Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh. The additions raise the total number of such wetlands in India.

A commercial communications satellite, BlueBird Block-2, was launched by ISRO for AST SpaceMobile, a company based in the United States. The satellite was launched on a commercial mission. The satellite is described as the largest commercial communications satellite deployed in Low Earth Orbit. Low Earth Orbit is preferred for Earth observation, communication constellations and hosting platforms such as the International Space Station.

In defence news, DRDO successfully tested the K-4 submarine-launched ballistic missile from INS Arighat. It also completed trials of the Akash-NG surface-to-air missile, produced with Bharat Electronics Limited.

Assam's Majuli hosts the Charaichung Festival, which promotes awareness of a protected royal bird sanctuary described as Asia's first. Majuli is recognised as the world's largest river island.

India marks International Cheetah Day on December 4. Project Cheetah, launched in 2022, marks the world's first inter-continental translocation of a large wild carnivore to reintroduce cheetahs in India. The International Cheetah Day was established by Dr. Laurie Marker to honour Khayam, the cheetah she raised.

questions.q: In which year was the Charaichung Royal Bird Sanctuary established? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the sanctuary was established in 1633 by Ahom ruler Pratap Singha.

questions.q: Siliserh Lake lies within the buffer zone of which tiger reserve? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Siliserh Lake is located within the Sariska Tiger Reserve buffer zone.

questions.q: Kopra Reservoir is situated in the upper catchment of which river basin? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet places Kopra Reservoir in the upper catchment of the Mahanadi River Basin.

questions.q: From which space centre did BlueBird Block-2 lift off? (name of the centre)
questions.explanation: The booklet says liftoff took place from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota.

questions.q: What is the mass of BlueBird Block-2? (in kg)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the satellite's mass as 6100 kg.

questions.q: Which commercial interface of ISRO facilitated the BlueBird Block-2 launch? (name or acronym)
questions.explanation: The booklet names NewSpace India Limited as the commercial interface of ISRO that facilitated the launch.

questions.q: Majuli, the world's largest river island, lies on which river? (name of river)
questions.explanation: The booklet places Majuli in Assam's Brahmaputra River.

quizzes.title: Silicon Initiative, Solar Irrigation and Treaties
quizzes.passage:
Pax Silica is a US-led strategic geo-economic and technology initiative. Its stated focus is building a secure, resilient and innovation-driven silicon supply chain. One of its key objectives is to reduce strategic dependencies on concentrated supply chains, while another is to strengthen technological leadership in semiconductors and AI.

SoLAR stands for Solar Irrigation for Agricultural Resilience. It aims to expand climate-resilient, solar-powered irrigation systems across South Asia and East Africa. The initiative seeks equitable and sustainable access for small and marginal farmers, and it promotes resilient agriculture under changing climate conditions.

On the 50th anniversary of the Biological Weapons Convention, India called for stronger global biosecurity, compliance and the promotion of peaceful uses of biological science. The convention is described as the first multilateral, legally binding disarmament treaty that eliminates an entire category of weapons of mass destruction. The convention is administered by the United Nations Office for Disarmament Affairs.

The Asian Development Bank works to promote sustainable, inclusive and climate-resilient economic development in Asia and the Pacific.

UNESCO, the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization, aims to foster shared humanity through education, science, culture and communication. UNESCO was established in 1945 and the organisation is headquartered in Paris, France. India has been re-elected to its Executive Board for 2025 to 2029.

questions.q: Which of the following countries is covered by SoLAR Phase II?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists India, Bangladesh, Kenya and Ethiopia as the countries covered by SoLAR Phase II.

questions.q: Which convention, adopted in 1960, is described as the first legally binding international treaty devoted exclusively to the right to education?
options: UNESCO Convention against Discrimination in Education
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the UNESCO Convention against Discrimination in Education as the first legally binding treaty exclusively devoted to the right to education.

questions.q: In the Kimberley Process, what term refers to rough diamonds used by rebel groups or their affiliates to finance armed conflicts against legitimate governments?
questions.explanation: The booklet defines conflict diamonds as rough diamonds used by rebel groups or their affiliates to finance armed conflicts against legitimate governments.

questions.q:
Read the two statements.
Assertion (A): India is excluded from the US-led Pax Silica initiative.
Reason (R): Pax Silica covers the entire silicon value chain, from critical minerals to chips, AI infrastructure and logistics.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet says India is excluded, and the value-chain scope is a separate fact that does not explain the exclusion.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Biological Weapons Convention (opened for signature)
II. Asian Development Bank (established)
III. India's chairmanship of the Kimberley Process (began)
IV. SoLAR Phase I (began)
A. 2019
B. 1972
C. 1966
D. 2026
questions.explanation: The booklet gives 1972 for the BWC, 1966 for the ADB, January 2026 for India's Kimberley chair, and 2019 for SoLAR Phase I.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Biological Weapons Convention prohibits the acquisition and transfer of biological and toxin weapons.
II. The Asian Development Bank is headquartered in Manila.
III. The ADB revised India's FY26 GDP growth forecast down to 6.5 per cent.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while the ADB revised the FY26 forecast upward to 7.2 per cent from 6.5 per cent.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Pax Silica's scope is limited to critical minerals and energy inputs.
II. SoLAR Phase I was implemented by the International Water Management Institute and the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation.
III. The Kimberley Process is a tripartite mechanism involving national governments, the international diamond industry and civil society organisations.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is wrong because Pax Silica covers the entire value chain, while statements II and III match the booklet.

quizzes.title: Institutions, Treaties and Global Bodies
quizzes.passage:
Pax Silica is a US-led strategic geo-economic and technology initiative. It focuses on building a secure, resilient and innovation-driven silicon supply chain, and its scope spans critical minerals, chips, AI infrastructure and logistics. Its key objectives include reducing strategic dependencies on concentrated supply chains.

SoLAR stands for Solar Irrigation for Agricultural Resilience and aims to expand climate-resilient, solar-powered irrigation across South Asia and East Africa. Its first phase focused on pilot interventions and on demonstrating solar irrigation models in South Asia. The initiative seeks equitable and sustainable access for small and marginal farmers.

The Biological Weapons Convention marked its 50th anniversary, and India called for stronger global biosecurity and compliance. The convention prohibits development, production, stockpiling and use of biological and toxin weapons. The convention is administered by the United Nations Office for Disarmament Affairs.

UNESCO is a specialised UN agency dedicated to fostering shared humanity through education, science, culture and communication.

The Asian Development Bank promotes sustainable, inclusive and climate-resilient economic development in Asia and the Pacific. In a recent update, it revised India's FY26 GDP growth forecast upward, from an earlier projection of 6.5 per cent.

The Kimberley Process is a tripartite global mechanism involving national governments, the international diamond industry and civil society organisations. The Kimberley Process aims to ensure that the global diamond trade does not fuel armed conflict or instability.

questions.q: Name the Gulf country that is a member of the US-led Pax Silica initiative. (country)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the United Arab Emirates among the members of Pax Silica.

questions.q: In which city is the International Water Management Institute, which implemented SoLAR Phase I, located? (city)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the International Water Management Institute is based in Colombo, Sri Lanka.

questions.q: In which city is the UN Office for Disarmament Affairs, which administers the Biological Weapons Convention, located? (city)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the UN Office for Disarmament Affairs as based in New York.

questions.q: In which city is UNESCO headquartered? (city)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the headquarters of UNESCO as Paris, France.

questions.q: Who is the Director-General of UNESCO? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet names Khaled El-Enany as UNESCO's Director-General.

questions.q: In which year did the Biological Weapons Convention enter into force? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Biological Weapons Convention entered into force in 1975.

questions.q: What percentage shareholding does Japan hold in the Asian Development Bank? (in per cent)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Japan as a major ADB shareholder with 15.6 per cent.
